model.name: DREAM S2 semantic news-cycle retention
model.lambda_interpretation: lambda = elapsed hours since semantic topic attention peak
model.abstraction_layer: Raw RSS articles are converted into stable semantic topic objects before S2 fitting.
model.semantic_layer: Sparse TF-IDF article vectors, entity sets, keyword distributions, semantic connected components, centroid inertia, and a persistent topic_memory.json file.
model.event_horizon_layer: H(t)=Deviation(t)*CrossScaleCoherence(t), with Deviation=observed/expected_S2 and CrossScaleCoherence from source-tier spread, source diversity, and semantic coherence. Pre-horizon alerts require high H and positive slope.
model.signal_preprocessing: Formal S2 fit uses circadian-corrected publish-time article counts: raw count divided by expected global publishing/activity factor.
model.observation_clock: article.published_at, not GitHub Action run time
model.history_role: data/history.json retains raw article records and first_seen/last_seen provenance; topic_memory.json retains semantic identity; cycles.json retains completed S2 cycle summaries.
model.comparison: Delta AIC = AIC(exponential beta=1) - AIC(stretched S2 beta free)
model.cycle_archive_role: data/cycles.json stores deduplicated completed formal cycle summaries so prior S2 learning remains visible when a new wave resets the current topic. Current waves are not archived until replaced by a new peak.

articles.title: Country diary: The light and shade of autumn’s shortening days | Merryn Glover
articles.summary: Loch Insh, Cairngorms: In my three decades in Scotland I’ve adjusted to the darkness of this time of year, and found glory in the quality of light It is the one clear day in a fortnight of heavy cloud, wind and rain, so I am out by the loch, basking in the rays of light, breathing them in, hoarding for the weeks to come. This time of year makes them all the more precious. Here in the Highlands, once we are past the autumnal equinox , we can almost feel the Earth tipping away from the sun as the light grows shorter each day and the night steals back. It’s a turn that is especially obvious when the clocks change and our evenings are suddenly dark. Continue reading...

articles.title: Crypto firms freeze more than $2.5bn in funds as Binance investigates potential hack
articles.summary: World’s largest crypto exchange said it had not confirmed whether funds had been pilfered Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, said on Thursday it is investigating reports of a potential security issue as its founder said the incident “does look like a hack on Binance”. The company said cryptocurrency firms had frozen more than $2.5bn in funds by Thursday evening. It wasn’t immediately clear the extent of the damage hackers might have been able to accomplish and Binance had not explicitly confirmed that funds had been pilfered, but stablecoin issuers quickly froze funds Thursday evening.
